Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Raj and I found the streaming demo helpful. Before we take this back to procurement and engineering, a couple of follow-ups from our side around performance/SLOs so we can finalize decision criteria: 

- Can you confirm p95 and p99 latency targets for both non-streaming and streaming flows (for payloads of ~512 tokens and ~2k tokens)?
- What throughput (requests/sec) and sustained concurrency (simultaneous sessions) can we expect from the hosted API vs Dedicated? We expect peak concurrent sessions in the 400–800 range during business hours; can Redwood handle that without excessive rate limiting?
- Do you support partial response streaming for long outputs (i.e., token-by-token streaming) with the same SLOs? Any caveats for WebSocket vs HTTP chunked streaming?
- Any recommended batching or KV cache configurations for conversation workloads to meet latencies under 300ms for p95 for short prompts?

Also: can you share a short SLO checklist or matrix we can include in our vendor evaluation sheet? Procurement is asking for a simple decision checklist (latency targets, concurrency tested, SLA terms).

Hi Raj — great to hear you found the streaming demo useful. Thanks for the clear list of asks. Below is a concise post-demo performance / SLO checklist and proposed next steps. I'm looping in Dev and Ethan for the technical specifics.

Post-demo SLO checklist (summary)
- Latency targets:
  - Short prompts (~512 tokens): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 200ms (hosted), p95 < 150ms (Dedicated reserved), p99 < 400ms
  - Long prompts (~2k tokens): p95 < 400ms (streaming enabled), p99 < 800ms
- Streaming: supported (token-by-token). For stable p95 while streaming we recommend WebSocket-based streaming for consistent connection/flow control; HTTP chunked streaming works but has slightly higher end-to-end jitter.
- Throughput & concurrency:
  - Hosted (shared): burstable to ~200 req/sec for medium models; sustained concurrency recommendations: up to ~200 concurrent sessions without elevated throttling.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): configurable; recommended baseline for your 400–800 peak concurrent sessions: 4–8 GPU pool (depends on model/quantization). We'll include mapping in the spreadsheet.
- Batching & caching:
  - Use continuous KV cache for conversation workloads; enables faster response for repeated context.
  - Adaptive batching (runtime) recommended; for sub-300ms p95 on short prompts we suggest conservative batching window (4–8ms) and small batch sizes when latency SLOs are strict.
- Fallbacks & rollouts: automatic fallback to smaller/quantized model variants if Dedicated pool saturated; graceful degradation settings available.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short SLO matrix and the demo recording (links below). Dev — see the attached latency_slo_matrix.xlsx for the numbers I promised.

Next steps / Mutual Action Plan (MAP)
1) Technical sync — Redwood infra + FintechCo infra (Ethan + Dev) — Friday, Oct 30 at 10:30am PT — owner: Marissa (confirm)
2) Shared SLO matrix & throughput mapping — owner: Dev Patel — due: Mon, Nov 2
3) Procurement checklist & high-level cost ballpark for Dedicated footprint — owner: Marissa — due: Wed, Nov 4
4) Pilot / POC scope (sample traffic patterns, datasets) — owner: FintechCo (Raj) — target: Nov 15

Let me know if you'd like the SLO matrix in a different format. We can also do a brief stress test with your example payloads during the sync if you want.

Best,

Raj — quick technical notes to supplement Marissa's checklist: 

- Measured numbers (baseline recommendations, 2k token sequence):
  - Dedicated (A100-style): ~900–1200 tokens/sec per GPU for inference at int8 quantization; latency p95 for streaming first token ~120ms, tail depends on context length.
  - Hosted: variability due to multi-tenant queuing — expect 10–25% higher p95 latency vs Dedicated under sustained high concurrency.
- Concurrency guidance:
  - If you need 400–800 simultaneous interactive sessions with streaming, we recommend Dedicated with 6 GPU-equivalents as a starting point. We can run a sizing test with your representative traffic to refine.
- Streaming specifics:
  - WebSocket streaming keeps back-pressure tight; HTTP chunked streaming is fine for demos but recommend WS for production streaming SLOs.
  - KV cache warmup: for conversation workloads, pre-warming the cache for active users reduces p95 significantly. Consider a short keepalive for active sessions.
- Suggested immediate deliverable: latency_slo_matrix.xlsx (attached) with rows for model variant, quantization, GPU type, expected p50/p95/p99, and recommended pool size.

I'll update the spreadsheet with an initial Dedicated sizing row today.

—Dev
